ROLE: observer
You review the results of an incident investigation. Write a short summary of what the latest results show, then update the list of hypotheses (at most 4, most likely first).

Root-cause categories:
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Each hypothesis has root_cause_category (one of the categories), rationale, and supporting_evidence_ids (only IDs that appear in the evidence below).

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"summary": "...", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "disk_full", "rationale": "...", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0123"]}]}

Alert: inventory-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 21:42 UTC)
Alerting service: inventory
Alert time: 2026-03-08T21:42:00Z
Data available from 2026-03-08T20:00:00Z to 2026-03-08T23:00:00Z

Evidence so far (the latest results are steps 4 onwards):
Step 1: metrics_query {"end": "2026-03-08T23:00:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-03-08T20:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check error rate evolution for inventory service over the incident window.)
  Result: M-023: Change detected at 2026-03-08T20:15:00Z: mean 0.47 before, 8.42 after (197.3 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-023] inventory.error_rate_pct from 2026-03-08T20:00:00Z to 2026-03-08T22:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.16 max=17.32 mean=7.76 last=17.17; mean=7.76. Change detected at 2026-03-08T20:15:00Z: mean 0.47 before, 8.42 after (197.3 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-03-08T20:15:00Z = 0.36 (first point after the change); 2026-03-08T20:25:00Z = 0.16 (lowest); 2026-03-08T22:15:00Z = 17.32 (peak); 2026-03-08T22:55:00Z = 17.17 (last).
Step 2: metrics_query {"end": "2026-03-08T23:00:00Z", "metric": "cpu_pct", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-03-08T20:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check CPU utilization for inventory service over the incident window.)
  Result: M-020: Change detected at 2026-03-08T20:15:00Z: mean 40.04 before, 38.23 after (4.5 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-020] inventory.cpu_pct from 2026-03-08T20:00:00Z to 2026-03-08T22:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=32.94 max=45.52 mean=38.38 last=44.67; mean=38.38. Change detected at 2026-03-08T20:15:00Z: mean 40.04 before, 38.23 after (4.5 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-03-08T20:15:00Z = 38.65 (first point after the change); 2026-03-08T21:10:00Z = 45.52 (peak); 2026-03-08T22:10:00Z = 32.94 (lowest); 2026-03-08T22:55:00Z = 44.67 (last).
Step 3: log_search {"end": "2026-03-08T21:45:00Z", "limit": 30, "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-03-08T21:35:00Z"} (asked because: Search inventory logs without level filter around the alert time to see what might have triggered errors.)
  Result: 16 matching log lines.

Step 4: metrics_query {"end": "2026-03-08T23:00:00Z", "metric": "db_pool_in_use_pct", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-03-08T20:00:00Z"} (asked because: Verify database connection pool usage percentage for inventory over the incident window.)
  Result: M-021: Change detected at 2026-03-08T21:20:00Z: mean 29.91 before, 86.87 after (18.4 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-021] inventory.db_pool_in_use_pct from 2026-03-08T20:00:00Z to 2026-03-08T22:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=24.96 max=100 mean=61.55 last=100; mean=61.55. Change detected at 2026-03-08T21:20:00Z: mean 29.91 before, 86.87 after (18.4 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-03-08T20:15:00Z = 24.96 (lowest); 2026-03-08T21:20:00Z = 36.82 (first point after the change); 2026-03-08T21:55:00Z = 100 (peak); 2026-03-08T22:55:00Z = 100 (last).
Step 5: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "How to resolve database connection pool exhaustion in inventory service"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook guidance for db_connection_pool_exhaustion to prepare mitigation steps.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-02-1 (similarity 0.73).
  [R-02-1] Database connection pool exhaustion - Summary (similarity 0.73): Requests to the database are waiting. The service has used up its whole allowance of database connections, so new work queues for a free connection and eventually times out before it ever reaches the database.
  [R-02-7] Database connection pool exhaustion - Escalation (similarity 0.73): Call the database team if the database itself is close to its connection limit or is refusing new connections, since raising pool sizes elsewhere will then make things worse. Share the pool graphs so they can see which services hold the most connections.
  [R-02-2] Database connection pool exhaustion - Symptoms (similarity 0.70): Latency climbs and errors follow as requests wait on the database and time out. Logs mention database timeouts and requests waiting. The service's CPU stays normal because it is idle while it waits, which can make the service look healthy from the outside.

Previous hypotheses:
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: Logs explicitly show HikariPool connection timeouts, all active connections in use, and inability to acquire JDBC connections. (evidence: L-0290, L-0292, L-0295)

response: {"summary": "Metrics and logs confirm that the inventory service experienced database connection pool exhaustion, with connection pool utilization jumping to 100% and logs showing HikariPool timeout errors and exhausted connections.", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "db_connection_pool_exhaustion", "rationale": "Logs show HikariPool connection timeouts, and metrics confirm database pool usage reached 100% leading to increased error rates.", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0290", "L-0292", "L-0295", "M-021"]}]}
